summary: City page (Wayback 2026-08-08; live page Cloudflare-blocked) read: $30/day confirmed (weekly/monthly/3-6-month rates), 30/50-amp, hot showers, Wi-Fi, booked by phone at City Hall. Waterfront riverfront -> creekside proposed (channel ~22-26 m). Phone added. Lead: Horseshoe Park Campground.
flags: Waterfront: riverfront -> creekside proposed. The South Branch Two Rivers is ~22-26 m wide at the campground on Esri imagery (440 m frame and z19 tiles), under the ~30 m riverfront line. The southern row of RV pads (centre ~48.7690,-96.9347) sits 10-15 m from the bank across mown grass and a low brushy fringe with a few trees at its west end - open enough for on-water, so creekside rather than a view. The city publishes no site map or numbers, so the river-side sites cannot be named; whether they sell by the night is not stated.
Phone: none stored -> 218-843-2737 (Hallock City Hall; the camping page's booking line, also Google's number).
Website hallockmn.org/camping/ is the city's page but answers a Cloudflare block ('Sorry, you have been blocked') to plain HTTP; read through Wayback (2026-08-08) - not retried by browser.

Long-stay check: the city posts nightly ($30), weekly and monthly rates and 3- to 6-month season rates with a 20% prepay discount. Google 4.4 stars from 16 reviews; reviews read describe week-long family stays and one '3rd year in a row we're here for the Sugar Beet Harvest' - a harvest-worker presence, but nothing says the park is mostly seasonal. Read as an ordinary city campground with long-stay options; no drop.

Hookups: a Google review says 'No water or sewage hook ups, but there is a dump station and showers at the entrance' (undated in the capture); the city page offers full water/sewer/electric only at Horseshoe Park, implying electric-only sites here. Water/sewer left unwritten (only a review states it).
Sites: stored count 48 came from old note prose; the city page gives no site count. Left as is.
Pin 48.77032,-96.93495 is at the park entrance; the camping loops centre ~48.7695,-96.9345 (~95 m), no move.
